requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: Types from referenced assemblies are deliberately not analysed or formatted by the compiling assembly (TypeCollector bails out on metadata-only types). This feature adds an explicit opt-in path that bypasses that rule through GeneratedFormatterCollector rather than TypeCollector, so L11 is not contradicted. It is recorded here as checked and fine.

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: New diagnostics MsgPack019-022 are added with docs, the index and AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md entries. Existing L4 severities are for other IDs, so there is no conflict. This also follows the convention of adding release notes.

Receipts/GeneratedFormatterHonoursTypeAttributesTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 2/2 failed

findings.claim: Attributes already on T are ignored, which breaks an acceptance criterion. With no SurrogateType, the collector always calls CreateContractlessMembers(type), which takes every public read-write member. It never checks T for [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember] or [DataContract]/[DataMember]/[IgnoreDataMember]. A member marked [IgnoreMember], or left out of a [DataContract], is still serialized. Keys are also member names instead of the declared Key/Order values, so the wire format differs from the dynamic resolver for the same type.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterHonoursTypeAttributesTests: both DataContractMembersAreHonoured and MessagePackObjectAttributesAreHonoured fail on head because the generated MyObjectFormatter source contains 'Secret'.

findings.claim: When the formatted type T has MessagePack or DataContract attributes, the generator ignores them. The requirement says these attributes must be honoured. With no surrogate, `CreateContractlessMembers` runs unconditionally and never reads T's attributes. As a result, `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key(n)]`, `[IgnoreMember]`, `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember]` and `[IgnoreDataMember]` on T have no effect. Every public read-write member is serialized under its name as a string key, including members marked `[IgnoreMember]`. Integer keys declared with `[Key(0)]` become string-keyed maps, so the wire format does not match T's declared contract.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptTests.AttributesOnFormattedTypeAreHonoured. ProjectA (emitted to an image reference) declares `[MessagePackObject] public class MyObject { [Key(0)] public int Value; [IgnoreMember] public int Secret; }`. ProjectB declares `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class MyObjectFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.MyObject> { }`. The test asserts that the generated formatter source does not reference `.Secret`. It fails on head.

findings.claim: The 'exactly one data type' rule that MsgPack020 states is not enforced. The guard only checks `formatterInterfaces.Length == 0`. A formatter that implements both `IMessagePackFormatter<A>` and `IMessagePackFormatter<B>` gets no MsgPack020. The generator silently uses `TypeArguments[0]` of the first interface and leaves the second interface unimplemented, which produces CS0535 in user code instead of the intended diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptTests.TwoFormatterInterfacesReportMsgPack020. The formatter implements `IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.A>` and `IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.B>`. The test asserts that the generator run result contains a MsgPack020 diagnostic. It fails on head.

findings.claim: the change's tests do not detect swap-boolean at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Analyzers/MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:324
the change's tests do not detect negate-condition at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/ObjectSerializationInfo.cs:168

hunches.claim: Contractless mode here differs from the library's existing contractless behaviour. Get-only public properties are silently dropped, because IsPublicReadWrite requires a public setter. Classes without an accessible parameterless constructor are rejected with MsgPack007, because constructorParameters is always empty. DynamicContractlessObjectResolver serializes readable public members and matches constructor parameters. Immutable library types, which are typical of a zero-dependency NuGet library, therefore get either an incomplete formatter or none.

receipt_plan.detail: Use a ProjectA type with 'public int Id { get; }' set via its constructor plus 'public string Label { get; set; }'. Serialize one instance with ContractlessStandardResolver and once with the generated MyObjectFormatter, then compare bytes: the generated output omits Id, or generation fails with MsgPack007 when only a parameterized constructor exists.

hunches.claim: GeneratedFormatterMustBePartial and the other new diagnostics are only reported from the generator via RegisterSourceOutput, not from the analyzer. Diagnostics reported from the generator are emitted on every generator run, not only in IDE analysis. A formatter with a SurrogateType that is invalid, such as mixed keys, yields no output and a diagnostic. The existing hook that skips hand-written formatter registration for attributed classes means such a class silently disappears from the resolver.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator snapshot tests with a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class that is non-partial. Confirm only the diagnostic appears and the resolver compiles.

hunches.claim: The contractless member key order is alphabetical by name (OrderBy Ordinal). The existing contractless behaviour in MessagePack, ContractlessStandardResolver, uses declaration or reflection order for maps. Bytes produced by the generated formatter therefore differ in key order from the dynamic contractless resolver for the same type. Deserialization is key-based so it still works, but byte equality and interop with existing contractless payloads is not preserved.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize a type with properties {Zeta, Alpha} using the ContractlessStandardResolver and the generated formatter. Compare map key order in the bytes.

hunches.claim: No test covers the private-member requirement or the combination of contractless behaviour with MessagePack attributes on T. The IsPublicReadWrite guard is only exercised by a read-only getter-only property (Doubled). Removing the public-setter or public-getter checks, or the field !IsReadOnly check, would survive because ExternalPerson has no private-setter, private, or readonly-field members.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:253 remove-guard: property.SetMethod is { DeclaredAccessibility: Accessibility.Public } -> property.SetMethod is not null; expected to survive because no test type has a non-public setter, only a getter-only property whose SetMethod is null.

hunches.claim: The requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes they are honoured. The collector ignores [MessagePackObject], [Key], and [IgnoreMember] on T itself and is always contractless unless a surrogate is given. No test puts attributes on the formatted type, so this requirement is untested and unimplemented.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a [MessagePackObject] type with [Key(0)] members and an [IgnoreMember] member, give it a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class, and assert the bytes use the integer keys. The test fails on head.

hunches.claim: The success-path guards in the collector are not covered: the parameterless-constructor check (NoDeserializingConstructor), the IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver handling and cast logic, and duplicate surrogate keys (KeysMustBeUnique). No test hits them, so deleting these branches would survive. The surrogate Key/IgnoreMember logic also has no test for a missing Key attribute (MemberNeedsKey).

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:76 remove-guard: delete the `if (isClass && !type.InstanceConstructors.Any(...))` block; expected to survive because no test uses a class without a public parameterless constructor.

hunches.claim: The GeneratedFormatterDataTypeNotSupported check is tested only for an abstract type. The generic, interface, and inaccessible-type branches have no tests, and neither does the MsgPack019/020/021 emission when the formatter is in a different file or nested.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:61 remove-guard: delete `|| !compilation.IsSymbolAccessibleWithin(type, formatter)`; expected to survive because only an abstract-type test exists.

hunches.claim: The GeneratorUtilities guard that excludes [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes from hand-written formatter registration has no direct test. The registration test, GeneratedFormattersAreRegisteredInGeneratedResolver, passes whether or not the guard exists, because it checks only the formatter type. Duplicate registration would only show up as a compile error or a snapshot difference, and no generator snapshot test exists for this feature.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratorUtilities.cs:38 remove-guard: delete the `!symbol.GetAttributes().Any(...)` clause; expected to survive or fail only through an incidental compile error, because no test asserts the resolver output.

hunches.claim: The surrogate int-key test only checks the array length of 8. It does not check the positions of the keys (3 and 7) or the nil gaps. Swapping IntKey values would pass because the round trip is self-consistent. The surrogate string-key path (CreateMember with stringKey: (string)key) has no positive test either.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:176 swap-boolean/off-by-one: in `CreateMember(target, intKey: intKey, ...)` use intKey+0 mapped to members.Count; expected to survive because the test checks only the header count and round-trips.

hunches.claim: The diagnostics tests only exercise the analyzer-side Collect path. Nothing asserts that the generator emits no output for a rejected formatter, and there is no positive generator snapshot test for the partial-class template branch (IsUserDeclaredFormatter ? "partial class" : ...). The execution tests cover only the contractless string-key and surrogate int-key templates, and only for public classes.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator snapshot tests and add a case for a user-declared formatter, to check the emitted partial class declaration, including a nested or namespaced formatter.

hunches.claim: `IsPartial` checks only the formatter's own declaration, not its containing types. If the formatter is nested inside a non-partial class, the generator still emits the nesting wrappers via `EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces` for the user's formatter name, which re-declares the outer type as partial. This yields a compile error such as CS0260 on the user's outer class, and MsgPack019 is not reported.

receipt_plan.detail: The `IsPartial` helper inspects only `formatter.DeclaringSyntaxReferences` and never walks `ContainingType`. The templates wrap the body in `EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces` using `Info.Formatter`, which is now the user-declared `QualifiedNamedTypeName(formatter)`. A test could declare `class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<X> { } }` and inspect the output compilation for CS0260.

hunches.claim: Four new Error-severity diagnostics (MsgPack019-022) are added to SupportedDiagnostics. They only fire for classes with the new attribute, so existing users are unaffected. However, the analyzer release tracking and docs are not updated in the shown hunks, and the helpLinkUri points to doc pages that may not exist. If AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md is missing the entries, RS2000 would break the repo build.

receipt_plan.detail: Check that AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md has MsgPack019-022 rows and that doc/analyzers/MsgPack019-022.md exist. Otherwise building the analyzer project with RS2000 enabled fails.

hunches.claim: The analyzer descriptors for MsgPack019-022 are registered in SupportedDiagnostics, but the diagnostics are reported only from the generator via RegisterSourceOutput. They are never reported by the analyzer's own Initialize code, so the analyzer-only package (L1) will not show them. The docs describe them as analyzer diagnostics.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Key and membership control comes from a new public SurrogateType property on GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute (the maintainer's surrogate suggestion). The surrogate's [Key]/[IgnoreMember] members are matched by name and type to T's members and validated with MsgPack022. Without a surrogate, T is always serialized contractless, regardless of any attributes on T.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Key control comes from T's own attributes (issue alternative 1 plus the maintainer comment), with no surrogate. Remove SurrogateType, CreateSurrogateMembers and MsgPack022. In GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect, if T has [DataContract], serialize only [DataMember] members, using Order as an int key or Name as a string key and skipping [IgnoreDataMember]. If T has [MessagePackObject], use its [Key]/[IgnoreMember] attributes. Otherwise fall back to CreateContractlessMembers.
